**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.

As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".

Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
On September 28, Toliver revealed the release date and cover art for _Life of a Don_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-35)_Life of a Don_ was released on October 8, 2021. The album included features from Travis Scott, Kali Uchis, SoFaygo, Baby Keem, and HVN.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-36) On February 24, 2022, Toliver appeared on a second track with West, "Broken Road" on West's album, _Donda 2_. On April 22, he appeared on Pusha T's song "Scrape It Off" from his album _[It's Almost Dry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_Almost\_Dry "It's Almost Dry")_ alongside Lil Uzi Vert. Exactly one week later, on April 29, he was featured on the single "Honest" by Justin Bieber, and the two artists performed it live for the Justice World Tour in Houston the same day and two days later in Dallas. On August 26, 2022, he was featured on DJ Khaled's album _God Did_ on the track "Lets Pray" along with Travis Scott. On September 9, he collaborated with Nav on the song "One Time" from his album _Demons Protected by Angels_ featuring Future. On November 18, he released the single "Do It Right".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-37) On December 2, he was featured numerous times on Metro Boomin's album _Heroes & Villains_ on the tracks "Too Many Nights" (with Future), "Around Me", and "I Can't Save You (Interlude) (with Future)".

### 2023–present: _Love Sick,_ _Hardstone Psycho_, and _Octane_
[edit]
On February 14, 2023, Toliver announced his third studio album, _Love Sick_. Following this announcement, the single "4 Me", featuring Kali Uchis, was released on February 15. On February 17, Toliver released the single "Leave the Club", featuring Lil Durk and GloRilla, and confirmed that _Love Sick_ would be released on February 24. The deluxe version of _Love Sick_ was released on February 28, 2023, including four additional tracks. Among these tracks were "Luckily I'm Having", featuring Teezo Touchdown, "Embarrassed", with labelmate Travis Scott, and "No Pole", the latter of which went viral on TikTok.
He was also featured on Kali Uchis' song "Fantasy", released on March 3 as part of her album, _Red Moon in Venus_. On March 12, 2024, Toliver announced his fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_. The album's promotion began with the release of the single "Bandit" on February 1. Following this, another single, "Deep in the Water", was released on March 15. On May 3, Toliver was featured on Yeat's single "Heavy Stunts".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-38) Later that month, on May 22, he released "Attitude" featuring Charlie Wilson and Cash Cobain, and announced the album release date the same day. _Hardstone Psycho_ was released on June 14.

### 2023–present: _Love Sick,_ _Hardstone Psycho_, and _Octane_
On July 13, 2025, Toliver, along with the other members of Jackboys, released the collaborative album, _JackBoys 2._ On September 5, 2025, Toliver released "Tiramisu" as the lead single for his new album, _Octane._ On January 22, 2026, Toliver released a trailer for the album on all social media platforms with a release date of January 30.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-39) On January 30, Toliver released _Octane,_ with 18 songs, such as "E85", "Rendezvous", featuring Yeat, "TMU", "Rosary", featuring Travis Scott, and "Body".
Toliver has cited his father, Sade, Dom Kennedy, Teddy Pendergrass, Paul Wall, Mike Jones, and Travis Scott as influences on his music.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)
He has been dating American singer Kali Uchis since 2020.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-40) In January 2024, he announced he was expecting his first child with Uchis; two months later, she gave birth to their son.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-42) On March 14, Toliver released the music video for his song "Deep in the Water", which was dedicated to Kali Uchis and their son.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-43)

On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)
texts.8:
### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
On September 28, Toliver revealed the release date and cover art for _Life of a Don_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-35)_Life of a Don_ was released on October 8, 2021. The album included features from Travis Scott, Kali Uchis, SoFaygo, Baby Keem, and HVN.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-36) On February 24, 2022, Toliver appeared on a second track with West, "Broken Road" on West's album, _Donda 2_. On April 22, he appeared on Pusha T's song "Scrape It Off" from his album _[It's Almost Dry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It's\_Almost\_Dry "It's Almost Dry")_ alongside Lil Uzi Vert. Exactly one week later, on April 29, he was featured on the single "Honest" by Justin Bieber, and the two artists performed it live for the Justice World Tour in Houston the same day and two days later in Dallas. On August 26, 2022, he was featured on DJ Khaled's album _God Did_ on the track "Lets Pray" along with Travis Scott. On September 9, he collaborated with Nav on the song "One Time" from his album _Demons Protected by Angels_ featuring Future. On November 18, he released the single "Do It Right".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-37) On December 2, he was featured numerous times on Metro Boomin's album _Heroes & Villains_ on the tracks "Too Many Nights" (with Future), "Around Me", and "I Can't Save You (Interlude) (with Future)".
texts.9:
### 2023–present: _Love Sick,_ _Hardstone Psycho_, and _Octane_
[edit]
On February 14, 2023, Toliver announced his third studio album, _Love Sick_. Following this announcement, the single "4 Me", featuring Kali Uchis, was released on February 15. On February 17, Toliver released the single "Leave the Club", featuring Lil Durk and GloRilla, and confirmed that _Love Sick_ would be released on February 24. The deluxe version of _Love Sick_ was released on February 28, 2023, including four additional tracks. Among these tracks were "Luckily I'm Having", featuring Teezo Touchdown, "Embarrassed", with labelmate Travis Scott, and "No Pole", the latter of which went viral on TikTok.
He was also featured on Kali Uchis' song "Fantasy", released on March 3 as part of her album, _Red Moon in Venus_. On March 12, 2024, Toliver announced his fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_. The album's promotion began with the release of the single "Bandit" on February 1. Following this, another single, "Deep in the Water", was released on March 15. On May 3, Toliver was featured on Yeat's single "Heavy Stunts".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-38) Later that month, on May 22, he released "Attitude" featuring Charlie Wilson and Cash Cobain, and announced the album release date the same day. _Hardstone Psycho_ was released on June 14.

On July 13, 2025, Toliver, along with the other members of Jackboys, released the collaborative album, _JackBoys 2._ On September 5, 2025, Toliver released "Tiramisu" as the lead single for his new album, _Octane._ On January 22, 2026, Toliver released a trailer for the album on all social media platforms with a release date of January 30.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-39) On January 30, Toliver released _Octane,_ with 18 songs, such as "E85", "Rendezvous", featuring Yeat, "TMU", "Rosary", featuring Travis Scott, and "Body".

Known for hit songs like No Idea and After Party, he has become one of the leading voices in modern melodic rap, building a global fanbase through his music, collaborations, and energetic live performances.

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.

As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".

Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)
He is featured on American rapper Eminem's January 2020 album, _Music to Be Murdered By_, on the song "No Regrets".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In February 2020, The Weeknd announced Toliver as an opener for his After Hours til Dawn Tour alongside Sabrina Claudio and 88Glam,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-After_Hours_Tour-26) however due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the tour was postponed and rescheduled without Toliver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-27)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

## About
Don Toliver is an award-winning, top-charting Houston-bred artist who delves in and out of genres to build all-engulfing worlds that are incomparable to any other. Whether soundtracking films, collaborating with peers like Travis Scott and Justin Bieber, or offering narrative-driven projects like _Heaven or Hell_ (2020), _Life of a DON_ (2021), _Love Sick_ (2023), and _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024), Don is a force in a lane all his own between hip-hop and cinematic R&B. Now, he’s back with _OCTANE_. Toliver’s fifth studio album is an explorative, grounding project that takes the listener on a full speed ride to the present, urging the listener to be present and enjoy life. Come along for the latest soundtrack to the adventure of life, which is ultimately “a long drive to a beautiful destination.”

Title: How Not to Be a Rap Star
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
March 6, 2008
Paul Mussan and Stelo X rolled into Atlanta’s Freight Room for the afterparty of BET’s _First-Annual Hip-Hop Awards._ There, someone told the Kansas City rapper and his manager that they’d need to buy $5 tickets to use for drinks at the bar.
Mussan wasn’t having it.
It was November 2006, and damn near every star in hip-hop’s firmament was descending on the Freight Room, a gala event space reserved for the night’s festivities. It was also Nelly‘s birthday, and the St. Louis rapper was set to perform live, along with Rick Ross and Jermaine Dupri. Snoop Dogg was there. Eve was there.
Mussan scanned the scene: 6-foot dudes stirring drinks in tiny plastic cups. He reached under his paisley designer hoodie, deep into the pockets of his jeans, pulled out five $100 bills and stuffed them in the palm of a passing event staffer. “I want bottles,” he said.
There were no tables set up in the ballroom, but minutes later, the waiters brought one. They set out bottles of Grey Goose and champagne. A bucket of ice. A case of orange juice. A couple of candles.
All eyes turned to Mussan.
“Motherfuckers were looking, like, Who the fuck is that?” Mussan recalls. “I’m looking at the rappers and shit, they got plastic cups in their hands. We’re walking around with big-ass Grey Goose bottles.”
As the night progressed, Mussan kept a bottle of vodka at his side and filled strangers’ cups. He took a picture with Snoop Dogg. Someone passed around Ecstasy, and people popped the pills like Altoids.
It felt like the peak of Mussan’s year, but 2006 was about to get even better. Radio stations around the country were starting to play his single, “59Fifty.” Kansas City’s top-rated radio station, KPRS 103.3, played it from December 2006 through February 2007. “People said he reminded them of 50 [Cent],” says the station’s program director, Myron Fears.
Mussan had the essential trinity for making it in the music industry: talent, connections and, thanks to a wealthy investor, money.

But it was starting to go to his head.
* * *
Mussan should have been Kansas City’s Nelly.
In 1999, a record exec’s map of America would have looked like this: pushpins up and down the coast of California. Pushpins in New York, in Atlanta, in Chicago. A pin in Houston. A pin in Miami.
When Nelly dropped his No. 1 hit album _Country Grammar_ in June 2000, the Midwest finally got its pin. On his way to fame, Nelly hauled his hometown with him, name-checking the Lou in effervescent party songs that looped on Top 40 radio. Nelly’s momentum carried the rest of his crew, the St. Lunatics, which released its own album (like Nelly’s, on Universal) the next year. Though St. Louis-born Chingy was a protégé of Ludacris, Chingy’s career took off after he went on tour with Nelly.
Kansas City’s hip-hop scene is still waiting for that kind of star. Many local artists blame KC radio, complaining that the city doesn’t have a station committed to pushing hometown music on regular rotation. (Charlie Chan, a DJ at St. Louis’ WHHL 104.1, broke Nelly by playing his singles in St. Louis clubs, which prompted DJ Kut to play him on New York City’s Power 105.1.)
Record execs are looking to break someone from the Midwest, says Terry McGill, CEO and founder of a Texas company called Major Money Entertainment. “That’s our goal — to put Kansas City on the map,” McGill tells _The Pitch_ by phone from his office near Dallas. “Not just Kansas City but the whole Midwest. Tulsa, Wichita, Kansas City, Omaha —there’s about four, five, six artists in those markets who have a shot. The key is just finding ’em.”
[page]
In the 1990s, McGill worked at record labels such as Motown and RCA. His résumé is dotted with old-school hip-hop royalty: Too Short, DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince, A Tribe Called Quest, KRS-ONE and Skee-lo. (Remember _I wish I was a little bit taller, I wish I was a baller_ ?)

These days, McGill is a consultant. He says he knows what sounds good in Brooklyn, what works in the Bay Area, what plays in the Dirty South. He creates an image and a marketing campaign for aspiring rap and R&B stars and shops their music to labels — for a fee. He says he knows the program directors at every urban radio station in the country, and he sends them music to test his clients’ potential hits.
In 2006, Mussan was one of McGill’s clients.
“The record was there,” McGill says of Mussan. “The record hit. I mean, we got it on the radio in several markets. A lot of artists, a lot of these guys, they’re young, and they start getting girls coming after them, fans start coming, and they get caught up. Their head gets big.”
* * *
Mussan moved to Kansas City in 1997. He’d been living with his father in California, and he wasn’t the type to be star-struck. At age 12, he says, he had a friend who landed a record deal as a “back-burner artist” and had minor roles in movies such as _Sister Act 2_. That friend’s manager used to sneak the teenage boys into clubs.
“Ice Cube was, like, my favorite rapper,” Mussan says. One night out, he bumped into his hero. “He looked at me like, What the fuck you doin’ here? I mean, ’cause I’m a fuckin’ kid in a nightclub. It was crazy.”
In Kansas City, where his mother’s side of the family lived, Mussan started performing in Westport nightspots as a rapper in 1998. “But I wasn’t shit,” he recalls with a shrug. “I was just one of the dudes that was there that had a verse on one of the songs someone was doing.” It took awhile for people to hear what he could really do, he says.
Mussan dropped mixtape after mixtape, rapping over well-known borrowed beats and including one or two original songs in the mix. Eventually, he found his own signature style.

During a lyricist’s battle at what was then Stanford and Son’s in 2002, Mussan advanced to the final round and faced a rapper called Stelo. (His real name is Melvin Artist.) Each was quick-witted and charismatic; the crowd picked Mussan as the winner in one round, Stelo in the next. The battle was a tie, and the rappers left the club with a mutual respect.
A few years later, Mussan showed up with friends to record at a Kansas City studio called Midgrange Music, and Stelo was there. The two former rivals became reacquainted. The more they talked, the more Mussan was convinced that Stelo was his key to navigating the music industry.
“I needed a manager, and he seemed to know what he was doing,” Mussan says.
Stelo had learned from Dallas hip-hop guru McGill. In 2000, Stelo was in Dallas performing with a rap group called High Style. Their unique sound and aggressive promotion caught McGill’s attention.
McGill had managed a group that included Frank Nitti and Don Vito, who both went on to produce platinum records. (Atlanta artist Yung Joc used a “Nitti beat” on his hit single “It’s Goin’ Down.” Don Vito recently produced the beats for three songs on an album by Jagged Edge, who is signed to Island Records.)
[page]
McGill remembers Stelo as the most talented rapper and writer in High Style, but the members of that group eventually went their separate ways. Then Stelo’s mother in Kansas City had a heart attack, so Stelo moved back and got a job at Tyson Foods in Olathe. During his off hours, he helped build the Midrange studio.

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.
texts.1:
As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".
texts.2: Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)
texts.3:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)
texts.4:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)
texts.5:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)
He is featured on American rapper Eminem's January 2020 album, _Music to Be Murdered By_, on the song "No Regrets".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In February 2020, The Weeknd announced Toliver as an opener for his After Hours til Dawn Tour alongside Sabrina Claudio and 88Glam,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-After_Hours_Tour-26) however due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the tour was postponed and rescheduled without Toliver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-27)
texts.6:
### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._
texts.7:
### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

## About
Don Toliver is an award-winning, top-charting Houston-bred artist who delves in and out of genres to build all-engulfing worlds that are incomparable to any other. Whether soundtracking films, collaborating with peers like Travis Scott and Justin Bieber, or offering narrative-driven projects like _Heaven or Hell_ (2020), _Life of a DON_ (2021), _Love Sick_ (2023), and _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024), Don is a force in a lane all his own between hip-hop and cinematic R&B. Now, he’s back with _OCTANE_. Toliver’s fifth studio album is an explorative, grounding project that takes the listener on a full speed ride to the present, urging the listener to be present and enjoy life. Come along for the latest soundtrack to the adventure of life, which is ultimately “a long drive to a beautiful destination.”

March 6, 2008
Paul Mussan and Stelo X rolled into Atlanta’s Freight Room for the afterparty of BET’s _First-Annual Hip-Hop Awards._ There, someone told the Kansas City rapper and his manager that they’d need to buy $5 tickets to use for drinks at the bar.
Mussan wasn’t having it.
It was November 2006, and damn near every star in hip-hop’s firmament was descending on the Freight Room, a gala event space reserved for the night’s festivities. It was also Nelly‘s birthday, and the St. Louis rapper was set to perform live, along with Rick Ross and Jermaine Dupri. Snoop Dogg was there. Eve was there.
Mussan scanned the scene: 6-foot dudes stirring drinks in tiny plastic cups. He reached under his paisley designer hoodie, deep into the pockets of his jeans, pulled out five $100 bills and stuffed them in the palm of a passing event staffer. “I want bottles,” he said.
There were no tables set up in the ballroom, but minutes later, the waiters brought one. They set out bottles of Grey Goose and champagne. A bucket of ice. A case of orange juice. A couple of candles.
All eyes turned to Mussan.
“Motherfuckers were looking, like, Who the fuck is that?” Mussan recalls. “I’m looking at the rappers and shit, they got plastic cups in their hands. We’re walking around with big-ass Grey Goose bottles.”
As the night progressed, Mussan kept a bottle of vodka at his side and filled strangers’ cups. He took a picture with Snoop Dogg. Someone passed around Ecstasy, and people popped the pills like Altoids.
It felt like the peak of Mussan’s year, but 2006 was about to get even better. Radio stations around the country were starting to play his single, “59Fifty.” Kansas City’s top-rated radio station, KPRS 103.3, played it from December 2006 through February 2007. “People said he reminded them of 50 [Cent],” says the station’s program director, Myron Fears.
Mussan had the essential trinity for making it in the music industry: talent, connections and, thanks to a wealthy investor, money.
texts.1:
But it was starting to go to his head.
* * *
Mussan should have been Kansas City’s Nelly.
In 1999, a record exec’s map of America would have looked like this: pushpins up and down the coast of California. Pushpins in New York, in Atlanta, in Chicago. A pin in Houston. A pin in Miami.
When Nelly dropped his No. 1 hit album _Country Grammar_ in June 2000, the Midwest finally got its pin. On his way to fame, Nelly hauled his hometown with him, name-checking the Lou in effervescent party songs that looped on Top 40 radio. Nelly’s momentum carried the rest of his crew, the St. Lunatics, which released its own album (like Nelly’s, on Universal) the next year. Though St. Louis-born Chingy was a protégé of Ludacris, Chingy’s career took off after he went on tour with Nelly.
Kansas City’s hip-hop scene is still waiting for that kind of star. Many local artists blame KC radio, complaining that the city doesn’t have a station committed to pushing hometown music on regular rotation. (Charlie Chan, a DJ at St. Louis’ WHHL 104.1, broke Nelly by playing his singles in St. Louis clubs, which prompted DJ Kut to play him on New York City’s Power 105.1.)
Record execs are looking to break someone from the Midwest, says Terry McGill, CEO and founder of a Texas company called Major Money Entertainment. “That’s our goal — to put Kansas City on the map,” McGill tells _The Pitch_ by phone from his office near Dallas. “Not just Kansas City but the whole Midwest. Tulsa, Wichita, Kansas City, Omaha —there’s about four, five, six artists in those markets who have a shot. The key is just finding ’em.”
[page]
In the 1990s, McGill worked at record labels such as Motown and RCA. His résumé is dotted with old-school hip-hop royalty: Too Short, DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince, A Tribe Called Quest, KRS-ONE and Skee-lo. (Remember _I wish I was a little bit taller, I wish I was a baller_ ?)
texts.2:
These days, McGill is a consultant. He says he knows what sounds good in Brooklyn, what works in the Bay Area, what plays in the Dirty South. He creates an image and a marketing campaign for aspiring rap and R&B stars and shops their music to labels — for a fee. He says he knows the program directors at every urban radio station in the country, and he sends them music to test his clients’ potential hits.
In 2006, Mussan was one of McGill’s clients.
“The record was there,” McGill says of Mussan. “The record hit. I mean, we got it on the radio in several markets. A lot of artists, a lot of these guys, they’re young, and they start getting girls coming after them, fans start coming, and they get caught up. Their head gets big.”
* * *
Mussan moved to Kansas City in 1997. He’d been living with his father in California, and he wasn’t the type to be star-struck. At age 12, he says, he had a friend who landed a record deal as a “back-burner artist” and had minor roles in movies such as _Sister Act 2_. That friend’s manager used to sneak the teenage boys into clubs.
“Ice Cube was, like, my favorite rapper,” Mussan says. One night out, he bumped into his hero. “He looked at me like, What the fuck you doin’ here? I mean, ’cause I’m a fuckin’ kid in a nightclub. It was crazy.”
In Kansas City, where his mother’s side of the family lived, Mussan started performing in Westport nightspots as a rapper in 1998. “But I wasn’t shit,” he recalls with a shrug. “I was just one of the dudes that was there that had a verse on one of the songs someone was doing.” It took awhile for people to hear what he could really do, he says.
Mussan dropped mixtape after mixtape, rapping over well-known borrowed beats and including one or two original songs in the mix. Eventually, he found his own signature style.
texts.3:
During a lyricist’s battle at what was then Stanford and Son’s in 2002, Mussan advanced to the final round and faced a rapper called Stelo. (His real name is Melvin Artist.) Each was quick-witted and charismatic; the crowd picked Mussan as the winner in one round, Stelo in the next. The battle was a tie, and the rappers left the club with a mutual respect.
A few years later, Mussan showed up with friends to record at a Kansas City studio called Midgrange Music, and Stelo was there. The two former rivals became reacquainted. The more they talked, the more Mussan was convinced that Stelo was his key to navigating the music industry.
“I needed a manager, and he seemed to know what he was doing,” Mussan says.
Stelo had learned from Dallas hip-hop guru McGill. In 2000, Stelo was in Dallas performing with a rap group called High Style. Their unique sound and aggressive promotion caught McGill’s attention.
McGill had managed a group that included Frank Nitti and Don Vito, who both went on to produce platinum records. (Atlanta artist Yung Joc used a “Nitti beat” on his hit single “It’s Goin’ Down.” Don Vito recently produced the beats for three songs on an album by Jagged Edge, who is signed to Island Records.)
[page]
McGill remembers Stelo as the most talented rapper and writer in High Style, but the members of that group eventually went their separate ways. Then Stelo’s mother in Kansas City had a heart attack, so Stelo moved back and got a job at Tyson Foods in Olathe. During his off hours, he helped build the Midrange studio.
McGill decided to make Stelo his protégé in Kansas City and told him to shop around for area artists who had potential.
Stelo found Mussan.
Mussan already co-owned an independent label, Final Track Records, with his friend Richard Coleman, who goes by the nickname “Milk.” (He’s Caucasian, with white-blond hair.)

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.

As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".

Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)

[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._

In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

Title: How Not to Be a Rap Star
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
March 6, 2008
Paul Mussan and Stelo X rolled into Atlanta’s Freight Room for the afterparty of BET’s _First-Annual Hip-Hop Awards._ There, someone told the Kansas City rapper and his manager that they’d need to buy $5 tickets to use for drinks at the bar.
Mussan wasn’t having it.
It was November 2006, and damn near every star in hip-hop’s firmament was descending on the Freight Room, a gala event space reserved for the night’s festivities. It was also Nelly‘s birthday, and the St. Louis rapper was set to perform live, along with Rick Ross and Jermaine Dupri. Snoop Dogg was there. Eve was there.
Mussan scanned the scene: 6-foot dudes stirring drinks in tiny plastic cups. He reached under his paisley designer hoodie, deep into the pockets of his jeans, pulled out five $100 bills and stuffed them in the palm of a passing event staffer. “I want bottles,” he said.
There were no tables set up in the ballroom, but minutes later, the waiters brought one. They set out bottles of Grey Goose and champagne. A bucket of ice. A case of orange juice. A couple of candles.
All eyes turned to Mussan.
“Motherfuckers were looking, like, Who the fuck is that?” Mussan recalls. “I’m looking at the rappers and shit, they got plastic cups in their hands. We’re walking around with big-ass Grey Goose bottles.”
As the night progressed, Mussan kept a bottle of vodka at his side and filled strangers’ cups. He took a picture with Snoop Dogg. Someone passed around Ecstasy, and people popped the pills like Altoids.
It felt like the peak of Mussan’s year, but 2006 was about to get even better. Radio stations around the country were starting to play his single, “59Fifty.” Kansas City’s top-rated radio station, KPRS 103.3, played it from December 2006 through February 2007. “People said he reminded them of 50 [Cent],” says the station’s program director, Myron Fears.
Mussan had the essential trinity for making it in the music industry: talent, connections and, thanks to a wealthy investor, money.

But it was starting to go to his head.
* * *
Mussan should have been Kansas City’s Nelly.
In 1999, a record exec’s map of America would have looked like this: pushpins up and down the coast of California. Pushpins in New York, in Atlanta, in Chicago. A pin in Houston. A pin in Miami.
When Nelly dropped his No. 1 hit album _Country Grammar_ in June 2000, the Midwest finally got its pin. On his way to fame, Nelly hauled his hometown with him, name-checking the Lou in effervescent party songs that looped on Top 40 radio. Nelly’s momentum carried the rest of his crew, the St. Lunatics, which released its own album (like Nelly’s, on Universal) the next year. Though St. Louis-born Chingy was a protégé of Ludacris, Chingy’s career took off after he went on tour with Nelly.
Kansas City’s hip-hop scene is still waiting for that kind of star. Many local artists blame KC radio, complaining that the city doesn’t have a station committed to pushing hometown music on regular rotation. (Charlie Chan, a DJ at St. Louis’ WHHL 104.1, broke Nelly by playing his singles in St. Louis clubs, which prompted DJ Kut to play him on New York City’s Power 105.1.)
Record execs are looking to break someone from the Midwest, says Terry McGill, CEO and founder of a Texas company called Major Money Entertainment. “That’s our goal — to put Kansas City on the map,” McGill tells _The Pitch_ by phone from his office near Dallas. “Not just Kansas City but the whole Midwest. Tulsa, Wichita, Kansas City, Omaha —there’s about four, five, six artists in those markets who have a shot. The key is just finding ’em.”
[page]
In the 1990s, McGill worked at record labels such as Motown and RCA. His résumé is dotted with old-school hip-hop royalty: Too Short, DJ Jazzy Jeff and the Fresh Prince, A Tribe Called Quest, KRS-ONE and Skee-lo. (Remember _I wish I was a little bit taller, I wish I was a baller_ ?)

These days, McGill is a consultant. He says he knows what sounds good in Brooklyn, what works in the Bay Area, what plays in the Dirty South. He creates an image and a marketing campaign for aspiring rap and R&B stars and shops their music to labels — for a fee. He says he knows the program directors at every urban radio station in the country, and he sends them music to test his clients’ potential hits.
In 2006, Mussan was one of McGill’s clients.
“The record was there,” McGill says of Mussan. “The record hit. I mean, we got it on the radio in several markets. A lot of artists, a lot of these guys, they’re young, and they start getting girls coming after them, fans start coming, and they get caught up. Their head gets big.”
* * *
Mussan moved to Kansas City in 1997. He’d been living with his father in California, and he wasn’t the type to be star-struck. At age 12, he says, he had a friend who landed a record deal as a “back-burner artist” and had minor roles in movies such as _Sister Act 2_. That friend’s manager used to sneak the teenage boys into clubs.
“Ice Cube was, like, my favorite rapper,” Mussan says. One night out, he bumped into his hero. “He looked at me like, What the fuck you doin’ here? I mean, ’cause I’m a fuckin’ kid in a nightclub. It was crazy.”
In Kansas City, where his mother’s side of the family lived, Mussan started performing in Westport nightspots as a rapper in 1998. “But I wasn’t shit,” he recalls with a shrug. “I was just one of the dudes that was there that had a verse on one of the songs someone was doing.” It took awhile for people to hear what he could really do, he says.
Mussan dropped mixtape after mixtape, rapping over well-known borrowed beats and including one or two original songs in the mix. Eventually, he found his own signature style.

During a lyricist’s battle at what was then Stanford and Son’s in 2002, Mussan advanced to the final round and faced a rapper called Stelo. (His real name is Melvin Artist.) Each was quick-witted and charismatic; the crowd picked Mussan as the winner in one round, Stelo in the next. The battle was a tie, and the rappers left the club with a mutual respect.
A few years later, Mussan showed up with friends to record at a Kansas City studio called Midgrange Music, and Stelo was there. The two former rivals became reacquainted. The more they talked, the more Mussan was convinced that Stelo was his key to navigating the music industry.
“I needed a manager, and he seemed to know what he was doing,” Mussan says.
Stelo had learned from Dallas hip-hop guru McGill. In 2000, Stelo was in Dallas performing with a rap group called High Style. Their unique sound and aggressive promotion caught McGill’s attention.
McGill had managed a group that included Frank Nitti and Don Vito, who both went on to produce platinum records. (Atlanta artist Yung Joc used a “Nitti beat” on his hit single “It’s Goin’ Down.” Don Vito recently produced the beats for three songs on an album by Jagged Edge, who is signed to Island Records.)
[page]
McGill remembers Stelo as the most talented rapper and writer in High Style, but the members of that group eventually went their separate ways. Then Stelo’s mother in Kansas City had a heart attack, so Stelo moved back and got a job at Tyson Foods in Olathe. During his off hours, he helped build the Midrange studio.
McGill decided to make Stelo his protégé in Kansas City and told him to shop around for area artists who had potential.
Stelo found Mussan.
Mussan already co-owned an independent label, Final Track Records, with his friend Richard Coleman, who goes by the nickname “Milk.” (He’s Caucasian, with white-blond hair.)

Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)
He is featured on American rapper Eminem's January 2020 album, _Music to Be Murdered By_, on the song "No Regrets".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In February 2020, The Weeknd announced Toliver as an opener for his After Hours til Dawn Tour alongside Sabrina Claudio and 88Glam,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-After_Hours_Tour-26) however due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the tour was postponed and rescheduled without Toliver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-27)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

# DON OMAR
... Read more Hey Lemon8 fam! So, I've been absolutely hooked on reggaeton lately, and one name just keeps popping up everywhere: Don Omar! You know, 'The King of Kings.' I was super curious to learn more about the man behind the music, and wow, what a journey of discovery it's been! If you’ve ever found yourself humming along to “Danza Kuduro” or “Taboo” and wondered about the artist, you're in the right place. First off, who is Don Omar? His full name is William Omar Landrón Rivera. He's not just a singer; he's a true multi-hyphenate artist – a versatile songwriter, rapper, record producer, and even an actor! He really is a powerhouse in the Latin music world, and his impact on reggaeton is undeniable. When people ask 'what is Don Omar,' it's clear he's more than just a musician; he's a cultural icon. Next, where is Don Omar from? This is a common question! Many people wonder about his nationality, and I've seen searches like 'is Don Omar Mexican?' or 'don omar from which country.' Well, he proudly hails from Carolina, Puerto Rico! This makes him a pivotal figure in the development and global popularization of reggaeton, a genre deeply rooted in the island's vibrant music scene. So, to answer definitively, yes, he is Puerto Rican! Now, let's talk about Don Omar's music genre. He is synonymous with reggaeton and Latin urban music. He's renowned for his incredible ability to blend diverse influences, from Caribbean rhythms to elements of hip-hop and electronic music. This unique fusion created a sound that captured the hearts of millions worldwide. Tracks like "Taboo" brilliantly showcase his talent for mixing tropical sounds with modern, infectious beats. His music genre is distinct, energetic, and always gets you moving. So, why is Don Omar famous? He earned the revered title 'El Rey' or 'King of Kings' due to his immense influence, innovative sound, and consistent string of global hits in the reggaeton scene. His debut album, "The Last Don" (released in 2003), was a monumental game-changer, featuring tracks like "Dale Don Dale" and "Dile" that became instant classics.

# DON OMAR
And, of course, who could forget the worldwide phenomenon "Danza Kuduro"? His powerful lyrics, electrifying stage presence, and genuine connection with audiences across the globe solidified his status as a living legend. These facts about Don Omar really highlight his impact. Beyond his music, some fun facts about Don Omar include his foray into acting, with appearances in the blockbuster Fast & Furious film series, which further expanded his global reach. His discography is extensive and critically acclaimed, featuring landmark albums like "King of Kings" (2006), which only further cemented his legacy in music history. He truly has consistently pushed the boundaries of Latin music, influencing countless artists and shaping the sound of a generation. Learning all these amazing facts about Don Omar really made me appreciate his artistry and dedication even more. If you haven't dived deep into his music, you're seriously missing out on some incredible tunes that will get your spirits up! What's your favorite Don Omar track? Let me know in the comments!
