**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.
texts.1:
As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".
texts.2: Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)
texts.3:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)
texts.4:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)
texts.5:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)
He is featured on American rapper Eminem's January 2020 album, _Music to Be Murdered By_, on the song "No Regrets".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In February 2020, The Weeknd announced Toliver as an opener for his After Hours til Dawn Tour alongside Sabrina Claudio and 88Glam,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-After_Hours_Tour-26) however due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the tour was postponed and rescheduled without Toliver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-27)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._
texts.7:
### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)
He is featured on American rapper Eminem's January 2020 album, _Music to Be Murdered By_, on the song "No Regrets".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In February 2020, The Weeknd announced Toliver as an opener for his After Hours til Dawn Tour alongside Sabrina Claudio and 88Glam,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-After_Hours_Tour-26) however due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the tour was postponed and rescheduled without Toliver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-27)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.

As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".

Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. **Genre:** Rap/Hip-hop
**Origin:** United States
Duality drives every Gemini. Born under this sign, Don Toliver naturally dips between extremes of pleasure and pain, mania and melancholy, and beauty and chaos. He does so by singing with stark soul (like a psychedelic Marvin Gaye) and woozily rapping through the haze of laidback anesthetized bars. As such, a distinct, dynamic, and diverse style defines his quiet movement to the forefront of the zeitgeist one trip at a time. Streamed hundreds of millions of times in under two years and handpicked for collaborations by everyone from “Big Bro” Travis Scott to Eminem, he emerges as the voice of 2020 — and beyond.
Don’s full-length debut, Heaven Or Hell [Cactus Jack/Atlantic Records], reflects every side of his sound widescreen.
“I’m trying to bring out the Gemini,” he affirms. “Life is Heaven Or Hell. You might be stuck in an office all day working, but then you go out and turn up in the club at night. I’m quiet in the studio, chilling, smoking, and writing. I get to the party, and I go crazy. So, the music is a roller coaster. There are happy and heartfelt feelings, but there are a lot of parties, drugs, and crazy shit you don’t see. Certain songs glorify the beautiful aspects of life. Others show the toxic environment. The music has each side. When you’re at home or on stage, it’s pure heaven. After the party ends, it doesn’t feel as pure. Nobody has had a chance to figure me out, so I’m giving them both Heaven Or Hell to answer some questions.”

He started posing those questions the first time he picked up a microphone. Born and raised in Houston, he found music at home as dad — going by “Bongo” — crooned the immortal chorus of Archie Lee’s H-Town classic “Swang Wide” [feat. Lil Mario, Big Tiger, BLNDCYDE, & Bongo]. Witnessing the business firsthand by hanging around pop’s homies Swishahouse co-founders Michael “5000” Watts and OG Ron, he also devoured records on his own. He regularly listened to Bobby Womack, Teddy Pendergrass, Sade, Kanye West, and Pharrell. Graduating from high school, he spent a couple years “hustling to pay for studio time,” making his introduction on the independent single “Pop The Seal.” He popped off in H-town first, taking over open mics, underground hotspots, art scene hangouts, and strip clubs. He found a perfect partner when fellow Houston native and platinum rapper Chedda Da Connect became his manager. The music made its way to Travis Scott in 2018, and the superstar signed him to Cactus Jack shortly after.
Don’s rise accelerated at lightspeed. He lent his voice to the platinum “Can’t Say” from Travis’s game-changing GRAMMY® Award-nominated triple-platinum, ASTROWORLD. Simultaneously, his mixtape Donny Womack attracted the praise of High Snobiety and Complex who named him on its “20 Rappers to Watch in 2019.” To cap off a banner year, he comprised JACKBOYS alongside Travis, Sheck Wes, and Chase B, igniting the #1 debut of the self-titled pack on the Billboard Top 200. The title Heaven Or Hell even stemmed from the JACKBOYS’ standout “Had Enough” where Don first said the line. Not to mention, Eminem tapped him to feature on “No Regrets” from his surprise comeback Music To Be Murdered By.
In the meantime, Heaven Or Hell single “No Idea” exploded. Don claimed #1 on the Billboard Emerging Artists Chart as the song moved into the Hot 100. Not only did “No Idea” generate 100 million-plus streams, but it also spawned millions of videos on TikTok and bulldozed a path for the arrival of the album by spinning a myth.

“I really want to create a myth,” he reveals. “If you get deeper and deeper into the music, you will end up in my world. There’s a chill vibe. It’s melodic hip-hop with rhythm and blues. It’s poetry for me. It comes from the heart and from my dreams coming true. Everything I’ve been through is inside of it.”
Heaven Or Hell exists on each end of the spectrum. “Wasted” hovers over a throwback beat on an intoxicating hook as it hypnotizes.
“Spaceship” blasts off on a grunge-y bounce as he pays homage to “Alicia Keys on my playlist.” Elsewhere, the unpredictable “Company” breaks into progressive rock guitar courtesy of super producer Mike Dean. The piano of “Euphoria” underscores gorgeous vocal interplay with Kaash Paige as it bleeds into the blissful chant, “Drowning in euphoria.”
Meanwhile, “Cardigan” represents the heavenly side with the unshakable refrain “You be on my back like a cardigan.”
“I’m talking about being in a relationship with a female,” he says. “It’s stressing me out, because she’s always bugging and on me like a magnifying glass.”
“I hope you feel beautiful chaos,” he leaves off. “Sometimes, you’ve got to be a little crazy in order to be great. I’m more excited to understand who Don Toliver is. I’ve had the liberty to sit back, watch, and still be me. I’m doing everything I always wanted.”
* * *

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.
texts.1:
As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".
texts.2: Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)
texts.3:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)
texts.4:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

Grammy-nominated artist and songwriter**Don Toliver**announces**NITROUS**the second leg of his blockbuster**OCTANE Tour.**Due to explosive fan demand and 31-city sold-out first leg**,**Don has added**19 new North American arena dates**and will bring the acclaimed production overseas for an**expansive run across Europe and the United Kingdom**this fall.
Produced by Live Nation and Cactus Jack,**the world tour will make a stop at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, PA, on September 3, 2026.**The tour will head overseas beginning October 25 in Paris, France, making stops across Switzerland, Italy, Germany, Poland, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Ireland, and the United Kingdom before concluding November 23 at The O2 in London. The sold-out first leg of the tour saw explosive performances from Don with several high profile guests including Travis Scott, SZA, Peso Pluma, Malcolm Todd and Sheck Wes.
Houston-bred, multi-platinum, and GRAMMY-nominated artist Don Toliver has solidified his status as one of music’s most innovative and boundary-pushing forces, masterfully blending hip-hop, rap, R&B, and cinematic storytelling to create immersive sonic worlds. Following a string of acclaimed projects including Heaven or Hell (2020), Life of a DON (2021), Love Sick (2023), and Hardstone Psycho (2024), Toliver entered 2026 with his career-defining fifth studio album, OCTANE.
texts.1:
The album exploded onto the charts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, earning Don his first solo chart-topper and delivering one of the biggest album debuts of 2026. OCTANE has since surpassed 1 billion streams on Spotify, making it the most-streamed hip-hop album of the year and solidifying “E85” and “Body” as the top two streaming hip-hop songs in 2026. Further cementing its cultural impact, all 17 tracks from the project landed simultaneously on Billboard’s Hot Rap Songs chart, making Toliver just the sixth artist in history to achieve 17 or more entries in a single week. Viral fan favorites including “E85” and “Body” continue to dominate streaming platforms and charts worldwide, fueling the album’s reign as one of the defining releases of 2026.
Don has also been featured on a slew of high-profile publications this year. From the covers of Billboard, Hypebeast, Flaunt and Boardroom, Don’s artistry and music industry takeover continues to be at the forefront of media. Complex named _OCTANE_ as one of the “best albums of 2026” claiming Don is in his “superstar era” while Spotify dubbed “E85” as one of the “songs of the summer.” Furthermore, Don will take center stage at this year’s BET Awards on June 28th where he is nominated for “Best Male Hip-Hop Artist”.
**TICKETS**: Tickets will be available beginning with the Don's Garage VIP Presale on Wednesday, June 24 at 10 am North America only). Fans can sign up at**DonToliver.com/tour**for access to the Artist Presale beginning on Wednesday, June 24 at 12 pm in all territories. Additional presales will run throughout the week ahead of the**general onsale beginning on Friday, June 26 at 12 pm at****LiveNation.com****.**
**DON'S GARAGE VIP PRESALE:**Fans in North America can get exclusive first access to GA and P1 tickets with the purchase of a Don's Garage VIP Package Bundle via Don's Garage VIP Presale on Wednesday 6/24 at 10am local. Limited inventory available. For more information, visit**vipnation.com**.

**Genre:** Rap/Hip-hop
**Origin:** United States
Duality drives every Gemini. Born under this sign, Don Toliver naturally dips between extremes of pleasure and pain, mania and melancholy, and beauty and chaos. He does so by singing with stark soul (like a psychedelic Marvin Gaye) and woozily rapping through the haze of laidback anesthetized bars. As such, a distinct, dynamic, and diverse style defines his quiet movement to the forefront of the zeitgeist one trip at a time. Streamed hundreds of millions of times in under two years and handpicked for collaborations by everyone from “Big Bro” Travis Scott to Eminem, he emerges as the voice of 2020 — and beyond.
Don’s full-length debut, Heaven Or Hell [Cactus Jack/Atlantic Records], reflects every side of his sound widescreen.
“I’m trying to bring out the Gemini,” he affirms. “Life is Heaven Or Hell. You might be stuck in an office all day working, but then you go out and turn up in the club at night. I’m quiet in the studio, chilling, smoking, and writing. I get to the party, and I go crazy. So, the music is a roller coaster. There are happy and heartfelt feelings, but there are a lot of parties, drugs, and crazy shit you don’t see. Certain songs glorify the beautiful aspects of life. Others show the toxic environment. The music has each side. When you’re at home or on stage, it’s pure heaven. After the party ends, it doesn’t feel as pure. Nobody has had a chance to figure me out, so I’m giving them both Heaven Or Hell to answer some questions.”

He started posing those questions the first time he picked up a microphone. Born and raised in Houston, he found music at home as dad — going by “Bongo” — crooned the immortal chorus of Archie Lee’s H-Town classic “Swang Wide” [feat. Lil Mario, Big Tiger, BLNDCYDE, & Bongo]. Witnessing the business firsthand by hanging around pop’s homies Swishahouse co-founders Michael “5000” Watts and OG Ron, he also devoured records on his own. He regularly listened to Bobby Womack, Teddy Pendergrass, Sade, Kanye West, and Pharrell. Graduating from high school, he spent a couple years “hustling to pay for studio time,” making his introduction on the independent single “Pop The Seal.” He popped off in H-town first, taking over open mics, underground hotspots, art scene hangouts, and strip clubs. He found a perfect partner when fellow Houston native and platinum rapper Chedda Da Connect became his manager. The music made its way to Travis Scott in 2018, and the superstar signed him to Cactus Jack shortly after.
Don’s rise accelerated at lightspeed. He lent his voice to the platinum “Can’t Say” from Travis’s game-changing GRAMMY® Award-nominated triple-platinum, ASTROWORLD. Simultaneously, his mixtape Donny Womack attracted the praise of High Snobiety and Complex who named him on its “20 Rappers to Watch in 2019.” To cap off a banner year, he comprised JACKBOYS alongside Travis, Sheck Wes, and Chase B, igniting the #1 debut of the self-titled pack on the Billboard Top 200. The title Heaven Or Hell even stemmed from the JACKBOYS’ standout “Had Enough” where Don first said the line. Not to mention, Eminem tapped him to feature on “No Regrets” from his surprise comeback Music To Be Murdered By.
In the meantime, Heaven Or Hell single “No Idea” exploded. Don claimed #1 on the Billboard Emerging Artists Chart as the song moved into the Hot 100. Not only did “No Idea” generate 100 million-plus streams, but it also spawned millions of videos on TikTok and bulldozed a path for the arrival of the album by spinning a myth.

“I really want to create a myth,” he reveals. “If you get deeper and deeper into the music, you will end up in my world. There’s a chill vibe. It’s melodic hip-hop with rhythm and blues. It’s poetry for me. It comes from the heart and from my dreams coming true. Everything I’ve been through is inside of it.”
Heaven Or Hell exists on each end of the spectrum. “Wasted” hovers over a throwback beat on an intoxicating hook as it hypnotizes.
“Spaceship” blasts off on a grunge-y bounce as he pays homage to “Alicia Keys on my playlist.” Elsewhere, the unpredictable “Company” breaks into progressive rock guitar courtesy of super producer Mike Dean. The piano of “Euphoria” underscores gorgeous vocal interplay with Kaash Paige as it bleeds into the blissful chant, “Drowning in euphoria.”
Meanwhile, “Cardigan” represents the heavenly side with the unshakable refrain “You be on my back like a cardigan.”
“I’m talking about being in a relationship with a female,” he says. “It’s stressing me out, because she’s always bugging and on me like a magnifying glass.”
“I hope you feel beautiful chaos,” he leaves off. “Sometimes, you’ve got to be a little crazy in order to be great. I’m more excited to understand who Don Toliver is. I’ve had the liberty to sit back, watch, and still be me. I’m doing everything I always wanted.”

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.

As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".

Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.

As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".

Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)
He is featured on American rapper Eminem's January 2020 album, _Music to Be Murdered By_, on the song "No Regrets".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In February 2020, The Weeknd announced Toliver as an opener for his After Hours til Dawn Tour alongside Sabrina Claudio and 88Glam,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-After_Hours_Tour-26) however due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the tour was postponed and rescheduled without Toliver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-27)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.
texts.1:
As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".
texts.2: Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)
texts.3:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)
texts.4:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)
texts.5:
### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)
He is featured on American rapper Eminem's January 2020 album, _Music to Be Murdered By_, on the song "No Regrets".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In February 2020, The Weeknd announced Toliver as an opener for his After Hours til Dawn Tour alongside Sabrina Claudio and 88Glam,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-After_Hours_Tour-26) however due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the tour was postponed and rescheduled without Toliver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-27)
texts.6:
### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._
texts.7:
### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.

As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".

Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

*   Rhythmic precision: strong sense of pocket and cadence; he rides beats with internal syncopation and strategic pauses.   
*   Versatility of flow: switches between rapid-fire bars, laid-back drawl, and sing-song hooks without sounding forced.
Writing craft
*   Concise storytelling: vivid, economical narratives that convey street detail, ambition, and consequence.   
*   Memorable lines and hooks: punchy one-liners and earworm choruses that translate to mainstream success.   
*   Structural control: songs move with clear setup, development, and payoff—verses and hooks are tightly constructed.
Authenticity and persona
*   Atlanta credibility: genuine Atlanta street origin story and role in the city’s rap ecosystem (trap’s development and gatekeeping).   
*   Consistent persona: “King of the South” image backed by lyrical content, interviews, and business moves—reduces cognitive dissonance between art and identity.   
*   Moral complexity: balances bravado with vulnerability and reflection, making his narratives feel lived-in rather than performative.
Innovator and style influencer

anye West has quickly emerged as one of the leading figures in hip-hop—a tastemaker in beats, rhymes, and fashion. His lyrical content spans everything from traditional themes like his own ego to subjects rarely if ever discussed in rap, like folding shirts at The Gap. Born in Atlanta to a Black Panther father and an academic mother, West moved to the South Side of Chicago at the age of three. West’s breakout moment came when he produced a number of songs on Jay-Z’s multiplatinum-selling The Blueprint (2001), including the lead single “Izzo (H.O.V.A.).” The following year West suffered a near-fatal car accident that left him with a metal plate in his jaw and an unbreakable resolve to become an MC. The result was The College Dropout (2004), with its vivid singles “Through the Wire,” “All Falls Down,” and “Jesus Walks.”

706 2000–2010—New Millennium Rap On The College Dropout, Kanye forged the constitutive elements of his style: sampling, fresh content, inventive wordplay, and transformative and slant rhyme–laden lyricism. For example, in “All Falls Down,” he rhymes “The concept of school seems so secure / Sophomore three years, ain’t picked a career,” altering his pronunciations of “secure,” “years,” and “career,” so that they all rhyme with an “-ur” sound. In subsequent years West’s strong personality and experimental style have helped define the cutting edge of hip-hop, both musically and lyrically. Infusing his rhymes with wit and lyrical density, and employing his skill as a producer to craft songs with complex beats and catchy samples, he has set himself apart with swagger but also with substance. *   Rhythmic precision: strong sense of pocket and cadence; he rides beats with internal syncopation and strategic pauses.   
*   Versatility of flow: switches between rapid-fire bars, laid-back drawl, and sing-song hooks without sounding forced.
Writing craft
*   Concise storytelling: vivid, economical narratives that convey street detail, ambition, and consequence.   
*   Memorable lines and hooks: punchy one-liners and earworm choruses that translate to mainstream success.   
*   Structural control: songs move with clear setup, development, and payoff—verses and hooks are tightly constructed.
Authenticity and persona
*   Atlanta credibility: genuine Atlanta street origin story and role in the city’s rap ecosystem (trap’s development and gatekeeping).   
*   Consistent persona: “King of the South” image backed by lyrical content, interviews, and business moves—reduces cognitive dissonance between art and identity.   
*   Moral complexity: balances bravado with vulnerability and reflection, making his narratives feel lived-in rather than performative.

anye West has quickly emerged as one of the leading figures in hip-hop—a tastemaker in beats, rhymes, and fashion. His lyrical content spans everything from traditional themes like his own ego to subjects rarely if ever discussed in rap, like folding shirts at The Gap. Born in Atlanta to a Black Panther father and an academic mother, West moved to the South Side of Chicago at the age of three. West’s breakout moment came when he produced a number of songs on Jay-Z’s multiplatinum-selling The Blueprint (2001), including the lead single “Izzo (H.O.V.A.).” The following year West suffered a near-fatal car accident that left him with a metal plate in his jaw and an unbreakable resolve to become an MC. The result was The College Dropout (2004), with its vivid singles “Through the Wire,” “All Falls Down,” and “Jesus Walks.”

Vocal presence and delivery
*   Commanding tone: a deep, authoritative voice that reads well on radio, clubs, and records.

*   Versatility of flow: switches between rapid-fire bars, laid-back drawl, and sing-song hooks without sounding forced.
Writing craft
*   Concise storytelling: vivid, economical narratives that convey street detail, ambition, and consequence.

*   Structural control: songs move with clear setup, development, and payoff—verses and hooks are tightly constructed.
Authenticity and persona
*   Atlanta credibility: genuine Atlanta street origin story and role in the city’s rap ecosystem (trap’s development and gatekeeping).

**Caleb Zackery** "**Don**" **Toliver**[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-2) ( _TOL-ə-vər_; born June 12, 1994) is an American rapper, singer and songwriter. His debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_ (2018), was released one day prior to fellow Houston rapper Travis Scott's album _Astroworld_, on which Toliver made a guest appearance. In the following week, he signed with Scott's record label, Cactus Jack Records, in a joint venture with Atlantic Records.

As a lead artist, he gained stronger recognition with his 2019 single, "No Idea" and his 2020 single "After Party", both of which entered the _Billboard_ Hot 100 and received triple platinum certifications by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Both songs first gained viral popularity on the video-hosting service TikTok, and preceded his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_ (2020). A critical and commercial success, it peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ 200 along with his second and third albums, _Life of a Don_ (2021) and _Love Sick_ (2023). He guest appeared alongside Nav and Gunna on Internet Money's 2020 single "Lemonade", which peaked within the top ten of the _Billboard_ Hot 100.
His trap-centered fourth studio album, _Hardstone Psycho_ (2024) peaked at number three on the _Billboard_ 200 and was led by the top 40 single, "Bandit". His fifth studio album, _Octane_ (2026) became his first number-one album and was supported by the singles "Tiramisu" and "ATM".

Toliver was raised in the Alief neighborhood of Houston, Texas.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) Alief is sometimes known as S.W.A.T. (South West Alief Texas).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) Performers such as Beyonce and Lizzo also came from this area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) He attended Alief Hastings High School.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:2-5) His father was a singer and rapper associated with independent Houston record label Swishahouse, and would commonly play music around him growing up.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-6) Don grew up listening to Michael Jackson and Usher.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) He was also influenced by listening to Swishahouse Classics.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
[edit]
Toliver's first release was a 2017 collaborative mixtape with Yungjosh93 titled _Playa Familia_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In late 2017, Toliver released the solo singles, "I Gotta" and "Diva".[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Elevator-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Respect-11) In March 2018, he signed to Atlantic Records and rapper Chedda Da Connect's record label We Run It Entertainment, in conjunction with Artist Partner Group. Also in early 2018, Toliver released "Make Sumn" and "Checks",[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Dream-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Trend-13) each accompanied with music videos. In July 2018, Toliver released the single "Holdin' Steel" featuring Dice Soho. The song was also accompanied by a music video.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-HNHHSteel-14) On August 2, Toliver released his major label debut mixtape, _Donny Womack_,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXMix-15) along with a music video for the song "Diamonds".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Fader-3) Travis Scott became aware of Toliver and invited him to many sessions.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:3-7) Toliver later called Scott "the OG,my CEO".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:4-8)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
The following day, on August 3, 2018, Travis Scott released his third studio album, _Astroworld_, on which Toliver was featured on the 13th track, "[Can't Say](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Can't_Say_(Travis_Scott_song) "Can't Say (Travis Scott song)")".[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-BB-1)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Complex-16) The single was later accompanied by a video that was sponsored by Yves Saint Laurent. On August 6, it was announced that Toliver had signed to Scott's Cactus Jack imprint label.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-DXCactus-17) Toliver appeared alongside Scott, Nav, Sheck Wes and Gunna in the music video for Nav's single "Champion", which Scott was featured on.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Snob-18) In September, his single "Diva" was later remixed by rapper Kevin Gates.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-19)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles
After his appearance on _Astroworld_, Toliver released several singles under the Cactus Jack label throughout 2019 including: "Back Up" featuring Wiz Khalifa,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-20) "Best You Had",[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-21) "Can't Feel My Legs",[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-22) and "No Idea".[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-23) The song "No Idea" eventually became a viral sensation on social media/video sharing platform TikTok. In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)
He is featured on American rapper Eminem's January 2020 album, _Music to Be Murdered By_, on the song "No Regrets".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9) In February 2020, The Weeknd announced Toliver as an opener for his After Hours til Dawn Tour alongside Sabrina Claudio and 88Glam,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-After_Hours_Tour-26) however due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the tour was postponed and rescheduled without Toliver.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-27)

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
[edit]
Toliver released his debut studio album, _Heaven or Hell_, on March 13, 2020, and with guest appearances from Travis Scott, Kaash Paige, Quavo, Offset, and Sheck Wes.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On May 8, 2020, Toliver was featured on Nav's song "Recap", from the latter's third studio album, _Good Intentions_.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-28) On July 24, 2020, Toliver and his DJ Chase B released a collaborative single titled "Cafeteria", featuring Gunna, from their upcoming collaborative project, _Escapism_. Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On August 14, 2020, Toliver was featured alongside Nav on "Lemonade" by Internet Money and Gunna, his first top 10 song on the _Billboard_ Hot 100 chart.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:0-4) On the same day, he was featured on Kaash Paige's song "Grammy Week", from her debut studio album, _Teenage Fever_. Exactly one week later, on August 21, he was featured alongside Big Sean on Nas' song "Replace Me", from his thirteenth studio album, _[King's Disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's\_Disease "King's Disease")_. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._

### 2020–2022: _Heaven or Hell_ and _Life of a Don_
In February 2021, Toliver teased his next project, titled _Life of a Don_, on Twitter.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-30) On May 4, Toliver released the lead single, "What You Need".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-31) One month later on June 18, Toliver released the second single from the album, "Drugs N Hella Melodies", featuring his girlfriend, American singer Kali Uchis.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-32) On August 20, 2021, Toliver released the single "[Don't Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Go_(Skrillex,_Justin_Bieber_and_Don_Toliver_song) "Don't Go (Skrillex, Justin Bieber and Don Toliver song)")", a collaboration with American record producer Skrillex and Canadian singer Justin Bieber.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-33) On August 29, Toliver appeared on Kanye West's album _Donda_ on the track "Moon", alongside Kid Cudi.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-34)

### 2017–2019: _Playa Familia_ and singles

In November 2019, Toliver accompanied Scott during the second Astroworld Festival.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-Astroworld_Festival_2019-24) On December 13, Toliver released the music video for "Can't Feel My Legs".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-25) Toliver featured on the December 2019 Cactus Jack compilation album _JackBoys._[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Toliver#cite_note-:1-9)

Exactly one week later, on July 31, he released a song titled "Clap", for the soundtrack of the film _F9_, in which the soundtrack was released on the same day, and the song became the seventh single. On October 22, he was featured alongside Gucci Mane on Rico Nasty's single "[Don't Like Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't_Like_Me "Don't Like Me")", from the latter's debut studio album, _Nightmare Vacation._
